title: Release engineering skeleton: versioning, changesets, signing placeholders
goal: Release engineering skeleton: Changesets-based versioning, build metadata stamped with the contract version, release channels, and signing/manifest scripts with placeholders. It produces dry-run artifacts only; publishing is added later.
scope_in: Changesets: `.changeset/config.json` with all `@centcom/*` packages in one `fixed` group (single product version), `changelog` plain, `access: restricted`, and `.changeset/README.md` explaining when to add a changeset.

`tools/release/build-meta.mjs` writing `dist/build-meta.json`: `{ version, contract_version (from contracts/index.json), commit, built_at (RFC 3339 ms UTC), channel: 'stable'|'beta'|'nightly', node }`; version rules: stable `x.y.z`, beta `x.y.z-beta.N`, nightly `x.y.z-nightly.YYYYMMDD`.

`tools/release/sign.mjs --file <artifact> --key-file <path>` producing `<artifact>.sig` (Ed25519 over `sha256:<hex>` of the file, base64url) and a CLI `--verify --pub <path>`; with no key it fails closed. A throwaway test key pair is generated inside tests only.

`tools/release/manifest.mjs` assembling a release manifest JSON (per platform+arch: url placeholder, sha256, size, sig, version, channel, min_client_version) shaped to the release-manifest schema from lane C003 output; platforms linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64, darwin-arm64, win32-x64.

`.github/workflows/release.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` only, `environment: release`, builds, runs build-meta, signs with a placeholder key from the environment secret `RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` if present, uploads artifacts, and does NOT publish to npm/Homebrew/CDN (steps are commented stubs with TODO issue links).
`docs/releasing.md`: versioning policy, channels, the dry-run procedure, key custody notes (key never in repo).
scope_out: Standalone binary building (Node SEA), installers, Homebrew tap, auto-update client: later packaging lanes.
CI checks: lane C002. The server side of the release manifest endpoint: the real backend.
Generating the manifest schema (lane C003 does).
build_against: Dry run only: tests use temp dirs, a generated Ed25519 test key and fake artifacts; the manifest is validated against the generated release-manifest validator.
interfaces: `node tools/release/sign.mjs --file F --key-file K` / `--verify --file F --sig S --pub P`; exit 0 ok, 1 verify fail, 2 usage/key error.
`node tools/release/manifest.mjs --channel C --dir artifacts/ --out manifest.json`; output fields mirror the release manifest contract.
`build-meta.json` is read by `userAgent()` callers (lane C003) to fill version and contract version.
acceptance: `build-meta.mjs` output for channel nightly on 2026-10-05 contains `version` matching `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+-nightly\.20261005$` and `contract_version` equal to contracts/index.json `contract_version`.
`sign.mjs` signature verifies with the matching public key and fails (exit 1) after flipping one byte of the file; signing without `--key-file` exits 2 and prints no key material.
`sign.mjs` refuses a key file with mode other than 0600 on POSIX (exit 2).
`manifest.mjs` lists exactly the 5 platform/arch pairs present in the artifacts dir, sorted deterministically, and output validates against the generated manifest validator.
Workflow `release.yml` contains no `npm publish`, `gh release create` or upload-to-CDN command outside comments (grep test), and runs only on `workflow_dispatch`.
`changeset status` passes on a PR that bumps one package and the fixed group bumps all `@centcom/*` to the same version.
tests: sign/verify (good, tampered, wrong key, bad perms).
guardrails: MUST NOT commit any signing key, even a test one; tests generate keys at run time.
MUST NOT publish anywhere in this lane; release workflow is dry-run and gated by the `release` environment.
Signature verification MUST use constant-time compare for digests and MUST verify before any artifact is trusted.
Build metadata MUST NOT include hostnames, usernames or absolute paths.
MUST pin third-party actions by SHA like CI (C002).
failure_modes: contracts/index.json unreadable -> build-meta exits 2; no artifact is stamped with an unknown contract version.
Missing platform artifact -> manifest exits 1 listing the missing platform/arch pair.
Key file unreadable -> sign exits 2 without touching the artifact.
